source.title: A Unified Approach to Controlling Implicit Regularization via Mirror Descent
source.authors: Haoyuan Sun; Khashayar Gatmiry; Kwangjun Ahn; Navid Azizan

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares mirror-descent variants on natural-label datasets and reports test performance, a conceptual test of how optimizer choice relates to generalization. It does not test the claim versions’ specific interventions or measures.
record.gate_note: The deep-learning experiments report test accuracy for p-GD variants and normalized versus fixed-step p-GD. Rows below capture those results. The paper's linear-classification results use synthetic data and classifier size or convergence measures, so they do not test the natural-label claim versions.
record.test_reason: Tables 10–11 bear on V3: the MNIST convolutional network has higher test accuracy than the fully connected network under every reported matched optimizer setting, including ordinary SGD. Although the experiments target normalized mirror descent, their architecture results bear on V3. Different training schedules and batch normalization prevent attributing the advantage specifically to local connectivity.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The central theoretical conclusion is directional convergence of mirror descent with homogeneous potentials to generalized regularized or maximum-margin solutions in separable linear classification. Neural-network experiments show different generalization performance across potentials, with p=3 highest in the reported CIFAR-10 and ImageNet tables, and improved MNIST accuracy with normalized updates. The authors leave a theory explaining the neural-network accuracy ordering for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Mirror descent with homogeneous potentials, including stochastic p-GD; the deep-learning comparisons vary p and compare normalized with fixed-step updates. The paper does not test the original claim versions' specified recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies with p and architecture on CIFAR-10; p=3 is highest for each of the four listed architectures. On ImageNet p=3 is highest for both architectures in one trial. On MNIST normalized updates exceed fixed-step accuracy for all reported p values and both architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing p changes CIFAR-10 and ImageNet accuracy; p=3 has the highest reported mean or single-trial accuracy for every tested architecture.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mirror-descent geometry affects held-out image-classification performance under the tested fixed hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized p-GD improves reported MNIST accuracy over fixed-step p-GD by 0.19–0.72 percentage points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-normalized p-GD improves final MNIST accuracy for the two architectures and three p values tested.

record.problems: ImageNet experiments are one trial per setting, do not reach 100% training accuracy, and omit weight decay; the authors estimate this costs around 3% validation accuracy in the p=2 case. CIFAR-10 reports averages and standard deviations over 5 trials. MNIST comparisons have no uncertainty estimates stated.
record.rows_left_out: Linear synthetic-data experiments measure convergence, classifier norms, or weight histograms rather than the listed natural-label claim-version outcomes. Figure-only training-loss and convergence plots are not included as separate rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed to interpolate.
The contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, convolution-derived initialization, and datasets beyond MNIST in the CNN–FC comparison.
Adam or comparable adaptive methods versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; switching optimizers and decoupled weight decay. Loss-normalized updates do not establish these comparisons.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed or adapted training budgets.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Removal of memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooks the V3 evidence available by comparing Tables 10 and 11. This is an incidental architecture comparison, with FC trained for 200 epochs and CNN for 50 epochs under different learning-rate schedules; it supports the observed accuracy ordering without isolating its architectural cause. Numerical values in all 42 rows match the supplied tables. No uncertainty is supplied for MNIST, and ImageNet uses one trial per setting.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test performance.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison isolating local connectivity.
No Adam or other adaptive-optimizer comparison with SGD under limited or broad tuning.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other measure of the training-test gap.
